Sabbath Observance
SAB-bath ub-ZUR-vuns
noun phrase (Christian ethics)
The biblical doctrine of the proper keeping of the Sabbath / Lord's Day. The Reformed-confessional position (Westminster Confession XXI.7-8) holds that one day in seven is to be kept holy unto God; the Sabbath moved from the seventh day to the first (the Lord's Day) in commemoration of Christ's resurrection; the day is kept by rest from worldly employments and recreations and by the public and private exercises of worship.

📖 Biblical Definition

The biblical doctrine of the proper keeping of the Sabbath / Lord's Day. The Reformed-confessional position (Westminster Confession XXI.7-8) holds: (1) the fourth commandment establishes a perpetual moral obligation to keep one day in seven holy unto God (Exodus 20:8-11); (2) the day moved from the seventh day (Saturday) to the first day (Sunday, the Lord's Day) in commemoration of Christ's resurrection (the apostolic pattern of first-day worship, Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2; Revelation 1:10); (3) the day is kept holy by a holy resting all that day from worldly employments and recreations, and by spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God's worship, except so much as is taken up in works of necessity and mercy (Westminster XXI.8). The Sabbath is grounded in creation (the LORD's rest on the seventh day, Genesis 2:2-3), in redemption (Israel's deliverance from Egyptian bondage, Deuteronomy 5:15), and in the new creation (Christ's resurrection on the first day). The Lord Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath (Mark 2:28) and clarifies that the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath (Mark 2:27) — correcting the Pharisaic legalistic accretions while affirming the substantive Sabbath principle. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive Reformed-confessional sabbatarian doctrine against both the antinomian position (the Sabbath is wholly abrogated; no day is holy) and the legalistic position (the Pharisaic-style multiplication of prohibitions). The substantive Sabbath observance: attendance at public worship (morning and evening where available); rest from ordinary labor and commerce; works of necessity and mercy permitted; the day given to worship, fellowship, rest, family worship, and the substantive enjoyment of the LORD.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Biblical doctrine of proper Sabbath / Lord's Day keeping; Reformed-confessional position (Westminster XXI.7-8): one day in seven kept holy, moved to the first day in commemoration of the resurrection, kept by rest from worldly employments and the exercises of worship; held against antinomianism and Pharisaic legalism.

SABBATH OBSERVANCE, n. phr. (Christian ethics) The proper keeping of the Sabbath / Lord's Day. Reformed-confessional position (Westminster XXI.7-8): (1) the fourth commandment establishes a perpetual moral obligation to keep one day in seven holy (Exodus 20:8-11); (2) the day moved from the seventh to the first (the Lord's Day) commemorating Christ's resurrection (Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2; Revelation 1:10); (3) kept by holy resting from worldly employments and recreations and spending the whole time in worship, except works of necessity and mercy. Grounded in creation (Genesis 2:2-3), redemption (Deuteronomy 5:15), new creation (Christ's resurrection). Christ is Lord of the Sabbath (Mark 2:28); the Sabbath was made for man (Mark 2:27). Held against antinomianism and Pharisaic legalism.

📖 Key Scripture

Exodus 20:8-11 — "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work."

Mark 2:27-28 — "And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath."

Isaiah 58:13-14 — "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable... Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD."

Hebrews 4:9-10 — "There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sabbath observance is held against two errors: antinomianism (the Sabbath is wholly abrogated; no day is holy) and Pharisaic legalism (the multiplication of prohibitions); the biblical doctrine is the substantive keeping of the Lord's Day in rest and worship.

expand to see more

Sabbath observance is held against two opposing errors. The antinomian position (the Sabbath is wholly abrogated as Old-Covenant ceremonial law; no day is holy under the New Covenant) contradicts the Reformed-confessional doctrine that the fourth commandment establishes a perpetual moral obligation grounded in creation (Genesis 2:2-3, the LORD's rest established the Sabbath principle before the Mosaic law). The Pharisaic-legalistic position (the multiplication of detailed prohibitions, the Sabbath as a burden of rule-keeping) contradicts the Lord Jesus's correction that the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath (Mark 2:27). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive Reformed-confessional doctrine: one day in seven kept holy unto the LORD; the day moved to the first (the Lord's Day) commemorating the resurrection; the day kept by rest from ordinary labor and commerce and by the exercises of public and private worship; works of necessity and mercy permitted; the day a substantive delight (Isaiah 58:13-14), not a burden — given to worship, fellowship, family worship, rest, and the substantive enjoyment of the LORD. The contemporary collapse of the Lord's Day into ordinary commercial-recreational activity is the substantive concern; the recovery of substantive Sabbath observance is a substantive mark of the patriarchal-Reformed household.
